title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp.17-19): Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, point-free 'analysis situs' for tame topology.

The data are:
- a set M of 'pieces' (morceaux), a set F (𝔉) of 'figures', and a set L of 'lieux', which are points/atoms;
- a refinement/part relation ≪, together with a weaker order ≤;
- a disjointness relation ∥ ('X and Y are apart') and its negation ∥̄ ('X meets Y');
- the 'shadow' Omb(X), the parts (or points) lying under X.

Axioms are labelled At… (AtD, AtC, Atpol, Atspéc, At fil, AtL1…). Here AtD is the heredity of disjointness to parts.

This page:
(1) Corollary 2 restates At fil, the existence of the sup of a filtered, locally finite family of refinements, for families increasing for ≪ instead of ≤.
(2) At supp, the 'axiom of supports of a refinement': let G ≪ X. If some Y ∈ M is disjoint from G but meets X, then such a Y can be chosen with Y ≪ X. So if X is not 'covered' by G, X has a part disjoint from G. In mereological language this is a weak-supplementation / remainder principle, phrased with ∥ instead of non-overlap.
(3) Margin variant, a localized strengthening: for a given Y with Y ∥ G and Y ∥̄ X, find Y' ≪ X with Y' ∥ G and Y' ∥̄ Y. He links this to the existence of 'good' neighbourhood-type pieces around G and defers it ('on y reviendra').
(4) Prop: the same holds with X replaced by any figure F ⊇≪ G.
(5) Question: if Y ∥ G and Y meets F, is there Y' ≪ Y with Y' ≪ F? AtD would then give Y' ∥ G. This is the requirement that 'meeting' implies 'having a common part'. Grothendieck calls this the 'good case'.
(6) He notes that, together with AtL1 (every piece contains an interior point), this would force, for a point x: x ∥̄ Y ⇔ x ≪ Y, i.e. x ∈ Omb(Y). Equivalently x ∥ Y ⇔ x ∉ Omb(Y). He judges this realistic only in 'set-theoretic' situations.
(7) He nevertheless records At ens D, the 'criterion of set-theoretic disjunction': X ∥ Y ⇔ Omb(X) ∩ Omb(Y) = ∅, i.e. no Z ∈ M with Z ≪ X and Z ≪ Y.

Next page draws the consequences: F ∥ G ⇔ disjoint shadows; for points, x ∥ y ⇔ x ≠ y; At ens D ⇒ At supp. He states that At supp holds in the frameworks he has in mind but At ens D does not.

The purpose is to separate disjointness ('not touching') from non-overlap. That is exactly what a contact/connection relation does as opposed to part-overlap, as needed for stratified/tame spaces where closed pieces can touch without sharing a piece.
errors: No outright error. The step 'Y' ≪ Y, Y ∥ G ⇒ Y' ∥ G' is AtD, as he says.

Claim (6) is only sketched. Deriving x ∥̄ Y ⇒ x ≪ Y from the 'good case' needs that a point has no proper parts, so that Y' ≪ x forces Y' = x. This is presumably among the point axioms (AtL…), but it is not stated here.
The margin variant is posed, not proved.

ideas.what: Axiomatization of space via pieces, a part relation ≪, a disjointness ∥ distinct from non-overlap, and points as a secondary layer
ideas.modern_name: mereotopology / contact algebras / Region Connection Calculus; point-free topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), de Laguna (1922), Clarke (1981), Randell–Cui–Cohn (1992), Düntsch–Vakarelov contact algebras
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only calls for an axiomatic tame topology; no axioms given

ideas.what: At supp: if G ≪ X and something meets X while avoiding G, then some part of X avoids G
At ens D: disjoint ⇔ no common part (disjoint shadows); rejected as unrealistic for intended frameworks
ideas.modern_name: identification of the connection relation C with overlap O (the 'set-theoretic' degenerate case of a contact algebra)

ideas.what: Sup of filtered locally finite families of refinements, version for ≪
ideas.modern_name: completeness/gluing axiom for refinements (cf. locally finite gluing in o-minimal/stratified settings)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axioms for tame topology are, in substance, a mereotopology. He distinguishes disjointness (∥) from non-overlap (empty common shadow) and explicitly rejects their identification (At ens D) for his intended frameworks. He keeps a supplementation axiom (At supp). This is precisely the contact-vs-overlap distinction of Whitehead/Clarke/RCC. That literature and the tame-topology literature (o-minimality, stratifications) appear never to have been connected through Grothendieck's notes.
missed.quote: Mais ceci n'est guère réaliste que pour les choses ensemblistes ... At ens D ... Pour que X ∥ Y, il (faut et) suffit que Omb(X) ∩ Omb(Y) = ∅
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could give a point-free axiomatics of tame/stratified geometry linking contact algebras (with their representation theorems) to o-minimal or semialgebraic frameworks, as Grothendieck's 'Esquisse' programme envisaged.

missed.claim: Localized supplementation is posed and deferred. Given Y apart from G and meeting X, find Y' ≪ X apart from G but meeting Y. Grothendieck ties this to the existence of 'good' neighbourhood-type pieces of G.
missed.quote: Pour Y donné, Y ∥ G, Y ∥̄ X, ∃ Y' ∈ M, Y' ≪ X, telle que Y' ∥ G, Y' ∥̄ Y ? ... On y reviendra
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an axiomatic shadow of regular-neighbourhood / tubular-neighbourhood existence in tame geometry.

deep.surprise_reason: These are unpublished, concrete axioms of Grothendieck's tame topology, close to mereotopological supplementation and contact principles. They are notable as a record, but technically elementary and partly tentative.
transcription_corrections: 'où Y est un ... lisse, dont a' probably reads 'dans le cas où Y est un lieu, disons x, et où la première question' (the following formula concerns a point x).
'Il en est [?] par At supp' likely 'Idem que At supp, avec X remplacé par F quelconque (G ≪ F)'.
'(⟸ est évident)' after x ∥̄ Y ⇔ x ≪ Y.
The line under x ≪ Y reads 'i.e. x ∈ Omb(Y)'.
In At supp, the struck text before G, X is 'F', and '{+(Y')+}' is an inserted alternative name for the new Y.
